Paycom pricing in 2026

Paycom publishes no price: its pricing page states only that pricing varies with workforce size and the tools chosen. One proposal is public: Paycom's 2026 proposal to Columbia County, Oregon, in the county board's 8 April 2026 agenda, priced its HCM solutions at $21.27 per employee per month for 210 employees, plus $8.63 per payroll run and $0.95 per check, a one-time conversion fee of $5,801.52, and increases of 0%, 4% and 5% over three years. That is one buyer's quote, not a list price. Ask Paycom for the same breakdown at your headcount and set it against the published rates in the ledger.

How the price is built

Ask which modules are bundled in the quote and which are separate lines, so the quote can be compared with a modular vendor.

What to get priced in writing

  • The per-employee rate for each module you take, as separate lines
  • Any monthly base or platform fee, stated separately from the per-employee rate
  • Whether any charge is per payroll run rather than per month, and the rate
  • The one-time implementation fee and what it covers
  • The contract term, any seat minimum, and the annual renewal increase cap in writing

For scale, the vendors that do publish an HRIS seat rate list from $3 to $29 per employee per month (every published rate). Enter your Paycom quote under “Your quote” in the ledger to set it against them over 3 years.

Does Paycom publish its prices?

No. The pricing page states that pricing varies based on workforce size and selected tools and services. The public example above is one county's proposal.

What should a Paycom quote break out?

The per-employee rate and what it covers, per-payroll-run and per-check charges, the one-time conversion fee, the contract term, any seat minimum and the annual increases. The Columbia County proposal shows all of these as separate lines.

What is Beti?

Paycom's payroll process in which employees review and approve their own paychecks before payroll is submitted. Ask whether it is included in the payroll price quoted to you.

How does Paycom compare with Paylocity on cost?

Neither publishes a price. The two public quotes we found were for different buyers and scopes: Paycom at $21.27 per employee per month for 210 employees (Oregon, 2026) and Paylocity at $20.66 for 112 employees (Utah, 2025). Ask both for the same breakdown at your headcount.
